acceptance_criteria.criterion: The `BodyRoute` interface no longer exists in `server.ts`; a `Route` interface with the `query?: URLSearchParams` handler parameter is exported instead.
No occurrence of `buildBodyRoutes` or `dispatchBodyRoute` remains in `server.ts` — all references use `buildRoutes` and `dispatchRoute`.
Existing body-route handlers that do not use query params continue to work unchanged (the `query` parameter is optional and ignored by existing handlers).
The dispatcher passes a valid `URLSearchParams` object to handlers; a handler accessing `query?.get('page')` receives the correct value from the request URL.
All existing tests that exercise routes via `handleRequest()` pass without modification.

summary: Renamed `BodyRoute` interface to `Route` and added optional `query?: URLSearchParams` third parameter to the handler signature in `mcp-server/gui/server.ts`.
Renamed `buildBodyRoutes()` to `buildRoutes()` with updated return type `Route[]`.

Renamed `dispatchBodyRoute()` to `dispatchRoute()`: changed the `path` parameter to `url` (full URL string), added `parseQueryString(url)` call to extract a `URLSearchParams` object, and passed it as the third argument to every matched handler.
Updated `handleRequest()` call site to call `dispatchRoute()` with `url` instead of `path`, ensuring the dispatcher receives the full URL including any query string.
Updated all JSDoc comments, section headers, and inline code comments throughout `server.ts` to use the new names — no occurrence of `BodyRoute`, `buildBodyRoutes`, or `dispatchBodyRoute` remains.
TypeScript check (`tsc --noEmit`) passes with zero errors. All 118 test files (3593 tests) pass without modification.

comments.note: The `dispatchRoute()` error log on line 1672 still uses the local `path` variable (derived from `url.split('?')[0]`) in the error message — this is correct and intentional, as logging the path without the query string is cleaner and avoids leaking sensitive query param values into stderr logs.

The `handleRequest()` function already had `const [path] = url.split('?')` for its own use by `matchRoute()`. Now that `dispatchRoute()` also does the same split internally, the local `path` constant in `handleRequest()` is only needed for the `matchRoute()` call — this is fine and not duplicated in a harmful way, but a future refactor could centralize the split once at the top of `handleRequest()` and pass both `path` and `query` to both dispatchers if the `matchRoute()` pattern is ever unified with the body-route table.

The route map summary block (lines ~1384–1454 in `matchRoute()`) is a manually maintained comment that duplicates structural information already encoded in the `buildRoutes()` table and `matchRoute()` conditionals. It will drift over time. A machine-readable route registry would eliminate this maintenance burden, but is clearly out of scope for this WP.

summary: Full Verification Stack executed against mcp-server/gui/server.ts.

AC1: `BodyRoute` is fully absent from server.ts (grep: 0 hits). `Route` interface exported at line 290 with `handler: (body: unknown, groups?: Record<string, string>, query?: URLSearchParams) => Promise<unknown>` signature. ✓
AC2: Zero occurrences of `buildBodyRoutes` or `dispatchBodyRoute` anywhere in the mcp-server/**/*.ts tree. `buildRoutes` (L1509) and `dispatchRoute` (L1636) are the sole implementations. ✓
AC3: All existing route handlers in `buildRoutes()` use only `(body)` or `(body, groups)` signatures — the optional `query` parameter is never referenced, confirming full backward compatibility. ✓

AC4: `dispatchRoute()` calls `parseQueryString(url)` on the full URL (line 1645) and passes the resulting `URLSearchParams` as the third argument to every matched handler (line 1658). `parseQueryString` correctly handles no-query URLs (returns `new URLSearchParams('')`), URLs with query strings, and empty-query URLs (`?` with nothing after). ✓
AC5: TypeScript compiler (`tsc --noEmit`) exits 0. All 118 test files / 3593 tests pass in 17.5s. No regressions. ✓

Edge-case audit: `parseQueryString` uses `indexOf('?')` guard, returning `new URLSearchParams('')` for no-query URLs — safe, no exceptions. Handler error path logs `path` (not raw `url`) to stderr on line 1672 — intentional and correct (avoids leaking query param values). `handleRequest` correctly passes the full `url` (not `path`) to `dispatchRoute` at line 1716, ensuring query params reach the dispatcher.

comments.note: No dedicated unit test exercises the `query` parameter injection path through `dispatchRoute()`. The current test suite verifies routes through `handleRequest()` integration-style, but there is no test that asserts a handler receives a correctly-populated `URLSearchParams` when the URL contains a query string. This is low-priority because the feature is a plumbing change and the implementation is simple and correct, but a targeted test would lock in the regression boundary when future route handlers begin consuming `query`.

summary: Reviewed mcp-server/gui/server.ts — the sole modified file.

Interface rename: `BodyRoute` → `Route` with `query?: URLSearchParams` third handler parameter is clean and correct. The old name was misleading (the table handles GET routes without bodies); the new name is accurate. JSDoc on the interface is complete and accurate.

`parseQueryString(url)` (L370–373): minimal, defensive, correct. Uses `indexOf('?')` guard correctly — returns empty URLSearchParams for no-query URLs, never throws. Does not use `new URL()` (which would require an absolute base) — the right choice for server-side path strings.

`dispatchRoute()` refactor (L1636–1680): calls `parseQueryString(url)` once at the function top (L1645) and passes the result to every matched handler (L1658). Route matching still uses the split `path` (L1644). Error log at L1672 correctly logs `path` (not `url`) to avoid leaking query param values in stderr. All correct.
`buildRoutes()`: all existing handlers remain at (body) or (body, groups) signatures — backward compat fully preserved. Infrastructure is ready for future handlers that consume `query`.
`handleRequest()` at L1716 correctly passes the full `url` (not `path`) to `dispatchRoute`, ensuring query params reach the dispatcher.

Dual URL split (once in `handleRequest` at L1697, once in `dispatchRoute` at L1644) is a mild DRY observation but not a problem: fixing it would require restructuring the function signature in a way that is out of scope and adds no correctness value.
All 5 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues found. One documentation-forward item recorded.

comments.note: Dual URL-split observation: both `handleRequest` (L1697) and `dispatchRoute` (L1644) independently split `url` on '?' to extract `path`. This is a minor DRY note — a future refactor could compute `path` once in `handleRequest` and pass both `path` and `url` to `dispatchRoute`. Not a blocker: the split is O(n) on a short string and correctness is unaffected. Noted for long-term maintainability awareness.

No blocking issues found — code is clean, minimal, and well-documented. The interface rename from `BodyRoute` to `Route` is a genuine improvement: the old name was misleading since the route table includes GET routes with `noBody: true`.

[documentation-forward] `parseQueryString` JSDoc (L366–373) documents the happy path and the no-query case, but does not mention edge cases: (1) a bare `?` with no trailing string (returns empty URLSearchParams — fine), (2) percent-encoded query strings (URLSearchParams decodes them — fine), (3) hash/fragment characters (passed through to URLSearchParams as literal chars — may or may not be intended). Adding a note about these edge-case behaviors would help future contributors who extend query-param handling.
